# Initial heap diagnostic checks compiler-emitted accesses independently of
# the package-state builder. These deliberately privileged test helpers attach
# runtime groups and expose foreign pointers; application transport cannot do so.
[short] skip
go build -gcflags=example.org/isolateheap=-d=isolateheap=1 -o heap.exe .
exec ./heap.exe own
stdout '^allowed$'
exec ./heap.exe host-read
stdout '^isolate: read from foreign heap$'
exec ./heap.exe host-write
stdout '^isolate: write to foreign heap$'
exec ./heap.exe instance-read
stdout '^isolate: read from foreign heap$'
exec ./heap.exe instance-write
stdout '^isolate: write to foreign heap$'
exec ./heap.exe peer-read
stdout '^isolate: read from foreign heap$'
exec ./heap.exe bulk-read
stdout '^isolate: read from foreign heap$'
exec ./heap.exe bulk-write
stdout '^isolate: write to foreign heap$'
exec ./heap.exe slice-read
stdout '^isolate: read from foreign heap$'
exec ./heap.exe slice-write
stdout '^isolate: write to foreign heap$'
exec ./heap.exe map-missing
stdout '^isolate: map read crosses owner boundary$'
exec ./heap.exe map-len
stdout '^isolate: map read crosses owner boundary$'
exec ./heap.exe map-range
stdout '^isolate: map read crosses owner boundary$'
exec ./heap.exe map-write
stdout '^isolate: map write crosses owner boundary$'
exec ./heap.exe map-delete
stdout '^isolate: map write crosses owner boundary$'
exec ./heap.exe map-clear
stdout '^isolate: map write crosses owner boundary$'
exec ./heap.exe chan-send
stdout '^isolate: write to foreign heap$'
exec ./heap.exe chan-recv
stdout '^isolate: write to foreign heap$'
exec ./heap.exe chan-close
stdout '^isolate: write to foreign heap$'
exec ./heap.exe chan-len
stdout '^isolate: read from foreign heap$'
exec ./heap.exe select
stdout '^isolate: write to foreign heap$'

# Level two also checks the references stored in an otherwise owned object.
go build -gcflags=example.org/isolateheap=-d=isolateheap=2 -o publication.exe .
exec ./publication.exe metadata
stdout '^allowed$'
exec ./publication.exe metadata-write
stdout '^isolate: write to foreign heap$'
exec ./publication.exe metadata-interior
stdout '^isolate: foreign heap reference publication$'
exec ./publication.exe own
stdout '^allowed$'
exec ./publication.exe publish-pointer
stdout '^isolate: foreign heap reference publication$'
exec ./publication.exe publish-slice
stdout '^isolate: foreign heap reference publication$'
exec ./publication.exe publish-interface
stdout '^isolate: foreign heap reference publication$'
exec ./publication.exe publish-closure
stdout '^isolate: foreign heap reference publication$'
exec ./publication.exe publish-bulk
stdout '^isolate: foreign heap reference publication$'
exec ./publication.exe publish-static
stdout '^isolate: foreign heap reference publication$'

-- go.mod --
module example.org/isolateheap
go 1.26
-- main.go --
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "os"
    "reflect"
    "unsafe"
    "example.org/isolateheap/bridge"
)

//go:linkname newGroup runtime.isolateNewGroup
func newGroup() unsafe.Pointer
//go:linkname setGroup runtime.isolateSetGroup
func setGroup(unsafe.Pointer) unsafe.Pointer
//go:linkname setOwner runtime.isolateSetOwner
func setOwner(uintptr) uintptr

type record struct { Data [64]int }
type holder struct {
    Pointer *record
    Bytes []byte
    Any any
    Function func() int
    Padding [64]int
}
var published *record
//go:noinline
func allocate() *record { return &record{Data: [64]int{11}} }
//go:noinline
func allocateTypes() *[7]reflect.Type { return new([7]reflect.Type) }
//go:noinline
func read(p *record) int { return p.Data[7] }
//go:noinline
func write(p *record) { p.Data[7] = 19 }
//go:noinline
func move(dst, src *record) { *dst = *src }
//go:noinline
func sliceRead(p []int) int { return p[7] }
//go:noinline
func sliceWrite(p []int) { p[7] = 19 }
//go:noinline
func tuple() (record, int, error) { return *allocate(), 27, nil }
//go:noinline
func tupleHeap(p *record, number *int, err *error) { *p, *number, *err = tuple() }
//go:noinline
func tupleReferences() (holder, int, error) {
    return holder{Pointer: allocate(), Bytes: []byte{7, 8}, Any: allocate(), Function: capture(39)}, 41, nil
}
//go:noinline
func tupleReferencesHeap(p *holder, number *int, err *error) { *p, *number, *err = tupleReferences() }
//go:noinline
func mapMissing(m map[string]int) int { return m["missing"] }
//go:noinline
func mapLen(m map[string]int) int { return len(m) }
//go:noinline
func mapRange(m map[string]int) { for range m {} }
//go:noinline
func mapWrite(m map[string]int) { m["key"] = 27 }
//go:noinline
func mapDelete(m map[string]int) { delete(m, "key") }
//go:noinline
func mapClear(m map[string]int) { clear(m) }
//go:noinline
func chanSend(c chan int) { c <- 27 }
//go:noinline
func chanRecv(c chan int) int { return <-c }
//go:noinline
func chanClose(c chan int) { close(c) }
//go:noinline
func chanLen(c chan int) int { return len(c) + cap(c) }
//go:noinline
func channelSelect(local, foreign chan int) {
    select { case <-local: case <-foreign: default: }
}
//go:noinline
func capture(value int) func() int { return func() int { return value } }
//go:noinline
func moveHolder(dst, src *holder) { *dst = *src }
//go:noinline
func publishStatic(value *record) { published = value }

func run(owner uintptr, fn func()) {
    group := newGroup()
    previousGroup := setGroup(group)
    previousOwner := setOwner(owner)
    defer setGroup(previousGroup)
    defer setOwner(previousOwner)
    fn()
}

func main() {
    host := allocate()
    hostMap := map[string]int{"key": 42}
    hostChan := make(chan int, 2)
    hostChan <- 11
    hostBytes := make([]byte, 16)
    hostFunction := capture(11)
    var owned *record
    run(101, func() { owned = allocate() })
    defer func() {
        if got := recover(); got != nil {
            // The rejected operation must not have mutated the host object.
            if host.Data[7] != 0 { panic("foreign write happened before checking") }
            if len(hostChan) != 1 { panic("foreign channel changed before checking") }
            if hostMap["key"] != 42 { panic("foreign map changed before checking") }
            if published != nil { panic("foreign reference escaped before checking") }
            hostChan <- 12 // A rejected close must not have closed this channel.
            fmt.Println(got)
        }
    }()
    switch os.Args[1] {
    case "metadata":
        run(104, func() {
            array := reflect.ArrayOf(1001, reflect.TypeFor[int]())
            record := reflect.StructOf([]reflect.StructField{{Name: "Value", Type: array}})
            types := []reflect.Type{array, record, reflect.PointerTo(record), reflect.SliceOf(record),
                reflect.ChanOf(reflect.BothDir, record), reflect.MapOf(reflect.TypeFor[string](), record),
                reflect.FuncOf([]reflect.Type{record}, []reflect.Type{array}, false)}
            target := allocateTypes()
            for i, typ := range types { target[i] = typ }
            for i, typ := range target {
                if typ != types[i] || typ.String() == "" { panic("metadata identity") }
            }
        })
    case "metadata-write":
        run(104, func() {
            typ := reflect.ArrayOf(1001, reflect.TypeFor[int]())
            root := reflect.ValueOf(typ).UnsafePointer()
            *(*byte)(root) = 0
        })
    case "metadata-interior":
        run(104, func() {
            typ := reflect.ArrayOf(1001, reflect.TypeFor[int]())
            root := reflect.ValueOf(typ).UnsafePointer()
            target := new(unsafe.Pointer)
            *target = unsafe.Add(root, 1)
        })
    case "own":
        run(102, func() { p := allocate(); write(p); if read(p) != 19 { panic("own state") } })
        run(103, func() {
            p, number, err := new(record), new(int), new(error)
            tupleHeap(p, number, err)
            if p.Data[0] != 11 || *number != 27 || *err != nil { panic("tuple result") }
            m := map[string]int{"key": 42}
            if mapMissing(m) != 0 || mapLen(m) != 1 { panic("own map") }
            mapRange(m)
            mapWrite(m)
            mapDelete(m)
            mapClear(m)
            c := make(chan int, 2)
            chanSend(c)
            if chanRecv(c) != 27 || chanLen(c) != 2 { panic("own channel") }
            channelSelect(c, nil)
            chanClose(c)
            if mapMissing(nil) != 0 || mapLen(nil) != 0 || chanLen(nil) != 0 { panic("nil semantics") }
            source := &holder{Pointer: allocate(), Bytes: make([]byte, 16), Any: allocate(), Function: capture(31)}
            target := new(holder)
            moveHolder(target, source)
            if target.Pointer != source.Pointer || target.Function() != 31 { panic("own references") }
            tupleReferencesHeap(target, number, err)
            if target.Pointer.Data[0] != 11 || target.Bytes[1] != 8 || target.Any.(*record).Data[0] != 11 || target.Function() != 39 || *number != 41 || *err != nil {
                panic("pointer-bearing tuple result")
            }
        })
    case "host-read": run(102, func() { read(host) })
    case "host-write": run(102, func() { write(host) })
    case "instance-read": read(owned)
    case "instance-write": write(owned)
    case "peer-read": run(102, func() { read(owned) })
    case "bulk-read": run(102, func() { move(allocate(), host) })
    case "bulk-write": run(102, func() { move(host, allocate()) })
    case "slice-read": run(102, func() { sliceRead(host.Data[:]) })
    case "slice-write": run(102, func() { sliceWrite(host.Data[:]) })
    case "map-missing": run(102, func() { mapMissing(hostMap) })
    case "map-len": run(102, func() { mapLen(hostMap) })
    case "map-range": run(102, func() { mapRange(hostMap) })
    case "map-write": run(102, func() { mapWrite(hostMap) })
    case "map-delete": run(102, func() { mapDelete(hostMap) })
    case "map-clear": run(102, func() { mapClear(hostMap) })
    case "chan-send": run(102, func() { chanSend(hostChan) })
    case "chan-recv": run(102, func() { chanRecv(hostChan) })
    case "chan-close": run(102, func() { chanClose(hostChan) })
    case "chan-len": run(102, func() { chanLen(hostChan) })
    case "select": run(102, func() {
        ready := make(chan int, 1)
        ready <- 1
        channelSelect(ready, hostChan)
    })
    case "publish-pointer": run(102, func() { p := new(holder); p.Pointer = owned })
    case "publish-slice": run(102, func() { p := new(holder); p.Bytes = hostBytes })
    case "publish-interface": run(102, func() { p := new(holder); p.Any = host })
    case "publish-closure": run(102, func() { p := new(holder); p.Function = hostFunction })
    case "publish-bulk": run(102, func() {
        source, target := new(holder), new(holder)
        // Deliberately bypass instrumented stores to manufacture the invalid
        // graph being tested. Its outer object still belongs to this instance.
        bridge.Set((*unsafe.Pointer)(unsafe.Pointer(&source.Pointer)), unsafe.Pointer(host))
        moveHolder(target, source)
    })
    case "publish-static": run(101, func() { publishStatic(owned) })
    default: panic("unknown test")
    }
    fmt.Println("allowed")
}
-- bridge/bridge.go --
// Package bridge is an uninstrumented test-only corruption helper.
package bridge
import "unsafe"
func Set(dst *unsafe.Pointer, value unsafe.Pointer) { *dst = value }
